restoration_note: Teaching describes how the Twelve Great Aeons of Light are reproduced as members within the spiritual man (five faculties + Calling/Hearing = seven), indwelt by the Living Spirit and centered on the Ambassador. Short editor restorations completing standardized phrases (Aeons, twelve, great, Light, the Five Elements, Pillar-of-Glory bearing the cosmos, Living Spirit with First Man, the foremost of the Aeons) are confidently confirmable from formula, parallels, and visible traces. Larger lacunae in the latter half (the struggle, the hidden chamber, the Ambassador's coming forth, the closing clause to 'unto the end of all the works') are too damaged or insufficiently constrained to restore responsibly and are left unrestorable.

restorations.basis: Editor restoration completing ⲛ̄[ⲁ]ⲓⲱⲛ 'Aeons'; single-letter completion confirmed by visible -ⲓⲱⲛ.
Standard formula 'Aeons of the Light' (ⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ); confirmed by surviving -ⲛⲉ at next line and parallel formulae throughout the doxology.
Editor completion of ⲡ[ⲙ]ⲛ̄ⲧⲉⲩ̈ⲧⲉ 'twelve'; single letter parallel to the same word in line 6.

Editor completion of [ⲛⲁ]ⲓⲱⲛ 'Aeons'; confirmed by visible -ⲓⲱⲛ and the third repetition of the doxological formula.

Six-character lacuna with no traces and no formulaic anchor; could be a connective or naming clause introducing the discussion of the lower Aeon at the foremost of the elements. Insufficient constraint.
Editor restoration; visible -ⲱⲛ at end confirms ⲁⲓⲱⲛ; ⲛⲁⲟ̄ is the standard Lycopolitan plural attributive matching the doxological 'great Aeons' of lines 6–8.
Editor restoration; standard Manichaean phrase ⲡⲧⲟⲩ ⲛ̄ⲥⲧⲟⲓⲭⲉⲓⲱⲛ 'the Five Elements' (= the Five Sons of the First Man); -ⲓⲭⲉⲱⲛ visible after gap; matches reading's 'five faculties of the First Man'.

Thirteen-character lacuna with damaged traces ([.]ⲕⲏ[. . . . . . . .] ⲧ . .) lacking a clear formulaic anchor. The clause introduces the dwelling of the Living Spirit, but the specific subject and grammar cannot be securely reconstructed.

Editor restoration; the Living Spirit/Omophoros-Pillar formula 'bears under the burdens of all the cosmos' is the standard Manichaean expression of the operative Divine power that orders the cosmos through the inner members; matches the reading's account of the Living Spirit ordering the All.
Editor restoration; the formula ⲡⲡⲛⲁ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄ 'the Living Spirit' joined with ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'the First Man' is the established pairing throughout the corpus and matches the reading's 'they are one'.

Editor restoration completing ⲥ[ⲙⲁⲙⲉ] 'blessing'; visible ⲡⲥⲙⲁⲙⲉ in the immediately following clause confirms the noun; ⲉⲧⲁϩ- relative perfect prefix fitting the syntax 'the blessing which has come unto them'.

Five-character continuation of a Greek loanword in ⲡⲣⲟⲥ-. Several candidates fit (ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲉⲩⲭⲏ 'prayer', ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲱⲡⲟⲛ 'face/presence', ⲡⲣⲟⲥⲃⲟⲗⲏ 'attack/onset'). The clause 'which is the cosmos established firm in him' does not uniquely select among them. Insufficient constraint.
Editor restoration; the phrase ⲡⲙⲛⲧⲉϩⲧⲉ 'the foremost' parallels lines 13 and 19–20, and ⲛ̄ⲁⲓⲱⲛ 'of the Aeons' is confirmed by visible -ⲱⲛ and the doxological formula governing the chapter.
Editor completion of ⲡⲟⲩⲁ[ⲓ̈ⲛⲉ] 'the Light'; the additional ~5 chars after this completion are too damaged for restoration and are left out.

Editor completion of ⲁⲩⲃⲁ[ⲗ]ⲟⲩ 'they were released' — single letter completing the verb ⲃⲱⲗ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ; English bracketed letters supply 'l' inside 'rele[l]eased' (the actual English completion is purely orthographic).

Editor brackets only ⲧⲭⲱⲣⲁ 'the region' as restored; the preceding ~4 chars are unconstrained, since 'which is not manifest' could attach to any of several hidden cosmological entities (mystery, hidden one, etc.). Insufficient anchor for the missing word.

Four-character lacuna following ⲧⲭⲱⲣⲁ 'the region' with no traces; could be a genitive modifier (e.g. ⲙⲡⲟⲩⲁⲓⲛⲉ, ⲙⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ) but the spiritual reading does not uniquely select one. Insufficient constraint.

Editor restoration adopting the idiom ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧⲟⲩ 'stand firm' (used immediately below in line 28 of the Ambassador) and completing ⲁⲩⲃ[ⲱⲕ] 'they went'; fits the reading's struggle-narrative 'lifted up against the Enemy'.
Five-character lacuna following ⲡⲭⲁⲭⲉ 'the Enemy' with no traces; no formulaic anchor sufficient to fix the continuation. Insufficient constraint.

Editor's own note marks the identification of ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲁⲓⲡⲧⲉ ('hidden chamber/repository?') as uncertain and the verb ending -ⲧⲱⲃⲓⲱ as a tentative reconstruction. With the head-noun's sense unsettled, the preceding ~5 characters cannot be securely restored.
Four-character lacuna after a relative ⲉⲧ-; the predicate of the relative clause about the 'hidden chamber' is unconstrained. Insufficient anchor.
Eight-character lacuna with only minor damaged traces preceding ⲡⲣⲉⲥⲃⲉⲩⲧⲏⲥ. Could be an introductory verb of sending, naming, or conjunction, but no formula uniquely fits.
Seven-character lacuna following ⲡⲓ̈ⲱⲧ ⲡ-; an epithet of the Father (possibly ⲛⲧⲙⲏⲉ 'of truth', ⲛ̄ⲧⲙⲛ̄ⲧⲛⲁⲟ̄ 'of Greatness', etc.) but no determinative trace narrows the choice.

Editor's tentative '[. . . . ⲁϩⲉ]' simply repeats the verb already visible in the line; the actual ~4 missing characters at the start of the line (likely a subject pronoun or connective for the Ambassador's coming) are not uniquely fixed.

Three-character lacuna after ⲛ̄ⲛⲉⲓ̈ 'these'; could be ⲁⲓⲱⲛ (Aeons), in keeping with the reading's center-of-the-Aeons motif, but a 3-char fill cannot reliably contain ⲁⲓⲱⲛ (4 chars) and no other equally short noun is firmly indicated.

Editor restoration completing ⲛ̄ⲁ[ⲓⲱⲛ ⲧⲏⲣⲟⲩ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲛ̄ⲛⲟⲩⲧⲉ] 'all the Aeons and the gods'; standard formula for the Father's title 'Father of all the Aeons and the gods' fitting the reading's identification of the Ambassador as 'beautiful Father of all the Aeons'.

Nine-character lacuna at the head of the closing clause '...unto the end of all the works' with no traces. Could be a temporal connective or final verb of fashioning, but unrecoverable from the given anchors.
